name: Refrigerant Integrity Plausibility
applicable_contexts: leak-rate history or refrigerant type unresolved
physical_basis: Refrigerant loss degrades capacity, raises kWh per ton-hour, and creates regulatory exposure (AIM Act phasedown for HFCs, SNAP rules, GHG reporting).
operational_basis: Top-up cylinders disguise loss-rate; the plant runs hotter and longer without visible alarm until capacity falls.
financial_mechanism: Leak-rate determines refrigerant CAPEX/OPEX trajectory under AIM, and operational kWh penalty. Misreading it skews retrofit timing.
typical_false_assumption: Refrigerant choice is permanent and not material to economics.
hypothesis: Refrigerant integrity is a plausible material loss-pattern requiring leak-rate evidence and regulatory phasedown framing.
rival_hypotheses: plant is tight and refrigerant choice is future-proof
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: leak rate above industry threshold or HFC phasedown applies
falsification_conditions: natural refrigerant (NH3/CO2) confirmed and audit on file
allowed_claim_language: Refrigerant integrity and regulatory phasedown exposure are plausible material issues requiring evidence.
financial_exposure_if_true: refrigerant replacement CAPEX accelerates under phasedown
stop_conditions: leak rate and refrigerant choice bounded
escalation_conditions: service provider leak audit if no documentary evidence
claim_permissions_impact: block refrigerant-agnostic financial logic when phasedown applies
example_outputs: Refrigerant integrity and AIM Act phasedown require leak-rate evidence before CAPEX framing.
tests: cold_chain bundle should activate this when refrigerant type/leak rate unresolved
